Glossary

# nous νοῦς

intellect; direct apprehension

Ancient Greek · glossed in English

[Glossary](https://www.philosophydef.com/glossary) / nous

A term is not a word. It is a working part of somebody's argument, and the English word usually offered for it is a compromise. This page gives the compromise, the argument, and the reading the sources do not support.

Where it is filed: [Mind](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/mind) · [Reason](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/reason) · [Understanding](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/understanding) · [Knowledge](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/knowledge) · [Being](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/being) · [Thinking](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/thinking)

## What the term does

Nous is the faculty by which first principles are grasped, as distinct from the discursive reasoning that works out their consequences. Aristotle says the principles of demonstration cannot themselves be demonstrated, so something must apprehend them immediately, and that is nous. Anaxagoras had made Nous the cosmic ordering principle, and Aristotle's unmoved mover is described as nous that thinks itself — the thought thinking thought, which is both the peak of his metaphysics and one of the most argued-about passages in the corpus.

## The reading the sources do not support

Treated as intuition in the modern psychological sense of a hunch. Nous is a cognitive achievement on the basis of training, not a feeling about what is probably true.
